A lot of whether a dating site is good it not is region-specific. In general, I find major cities have a lot more good looking members than rural areas. Not sure if it's just a numbers game or if rural people are hammier.

In OKC, the site keeps track of how many people are interested in you. The algorithm changes over the years, but basically it increases its rating of your attractiveness based on how many people who see you go on to like you and/or visit your profile. Your attractiveness affects who sees you and who you see, which (in theory) should minimize the number of unwanted advances people deal with from members who are uglier than they are. The people you're seeing now are either brand-new or (more likely) unattractive enough that they never graduated from the bottom tier of attractiveness.

Assuming your profile is okay, you just have to wait it out. You won't see as many visitors as a woman would, but you can speed things up by logging in and changing the wording of something tiny in your profile. The edit will temporarily boost your exposure a little.

If you don't have a great profile (if you just made it, you probably don't), you can kill two birds with one stone by making actual edits, instead. Most men don't go around photographing themselves, especially when single, so your best bang for your buck may well be to work on getting a good set of photos together. Barring that, the text of your profile is maybe half as important, but it's easier to work on.

In general, try to keep your profile brief, lightly humorous, and informative enough to let a woman sketch an outline of you without reading like a dossier or having enough information to stifle typical first date conversations. If you're organized, use bullet points instead of paragraphs.

Text:

  1. Really limit the "favorites" section because it's boring and can get bloated really quickly.
  2. An easy place to be a little creative and funny is on the "things I couldn't do without." Your goal is to entertain while summarizing yourself, not to try out for Survivor.
  3. Ditto for the section on admitting a secret. Write something a little funny and surprising.
  4. Be candid in the "message me if" section. I don't go full FPH because a lot of (human) women have body issues and will react like your stance applies to them. But you could say you "lead an active lifestyle and are looking for someone who can keep up," or something to that effect.
  5. If a section has more than 2-3 sentences, it's probably too long.

Photos:

  1. Full Body Shot. Basically, prove you're not fat. Take it head-on, and preferably not in a mirror.
  2. Friends. Prove you have a social life, show the sort of people you hang out with.
  3. Smile. Try to include one where you're laughing or at least smiling so she can see you having fun and see your teeth. This may be especially important for you if you have a scarred/scary look.
  4. Hobbies. If you have hobbies that bring you out of your house, get photos of yourself doing those hobbies. Ideally, have a few of these in total, from different occasions. Active people are way more attractive than couch potatoes, and lighting makes your photos look much better outside.
  5. The Preview. Photo of you doing something date-y (at a bar or restaurant, usually) and having a good time, preferably taken by someone sitting across from you. This primes your visitors to imagine a date with you. They imagine that they're having a good time, because you are in the photo.
  6. Lifestyle/Values/Service. Do you spend a lot of time with a given family member? Have a pet? Volunteer as a scout leader or at a church? Get a photo. In addition to being informative, this characterizes you as an empathetic person, which most woman find attractive. Again, this may be more important for you if your scars make you look intimidating

Anyway, online dating sucks, but I've had a fair amount of success with it. The above applies pretty well on most apps. A good profile sets itself apart because it attracts, entertains, and leaves the reader wanting to learn more about its author. In general, respond to prompts within the context of that overall intent instead of just filling in the blanks. Good luck out there.
